title: Introduce quantile-ensemble with traffic-conditioned smoothing guard
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: Canary detectors currently compare single-slice quantiles and can be noisy when traffic mix shifts or when cohorts are small. This change introduces a quantile-ensemble fusion and a traffic-conditioned smoothing guard that (1) synthesizes stable percentile estimates across traffic slices, (2) applies adaptive temporal smoothing when traffic modal changes are detected, and (3) gates rollouts if cross-slice divergence indicates a likely coverage/regression risk.

What this PR does: Adds a QuantileEnsemble detector and TrafficSmoothingGuard into the canary pipeline. Core behaviors: - Per-slice quantile estimators (p10/p50/p90/p95/p99) are fused via a weighted ensemble that accounts for slice sampling variance and recent throughput stability. - A traffic-modal detector watches for rapid changes in slice weights (e.g., geometry of client cohorts). When modal shifts occur, the smoothing parameter alpha is increased to avoid chasing transient spikes. - Cross-slice divergence score: a normalized L1 between slice quantiles; if score exceeds threshold and persists for N windows, the TrafficSmoothingGuard halts automated cutover and signals a canary rollback path. - Synthetic probe scheduler updated to bias probes toward under-sampled slices during canary windows so ensemble estimates converge faster. - New dashboard panels and alerting rules for ensemble spread, smoothing alpha, and guard trips.

Why this approach: Ensemble fusion mitigates brittle single-slice alarms during natural traffic churn and maintains sensitivity to true regressions. Traffic-conditioned smoothing avoids both overreacting to transient shifts and underreacting when the system has genuinely changed.

Commits summary: - 3fd2b1c: add quantile ensemble core and weighting scheme - 9a7b4e2: implement traffic-modal detector and smoothing controller - c2f4a9d: integrate guard into canary pipeline and add cutover veto logic - b5e7f88: update synthetic probe scheduler & tests - e1d9b02: dashboards, alerts, runbook additions and docs

Files changed (high level): - src/canary/detectors/quantile_ensemble.py (core estimator + fusion) - src/canary/guards/traffic_smoothing_guard.py (guard + threshold logic) - src/canary/probes/synthetic_scheduler.py (biasing to under-sampled slices) - tests/unit/test_quantile_ensemble.py - tests/integration/test_traffic_smoothing_guard.py - dashboards/perf_canary/ensemble_panels.json - ops/runbooks/canary_ensemble_guard.md - ci/pipelines/canary-suite.yaml

Example pseudo behavior (single paragraph): During a rollout to 20% traffic split across three cohorts, the quantile ensemble computes per-slice p95 with variance-aware weights (larger weight to stable slices). If a client-side traffic spike shifts 40% of requests into a small cohort for two windows, the modal detector raises the smoothing alpha from 0.2 to 0.6; ensemble updates then favor temporal smoothing and the guard will block cutover if cross-slice divergence remains high for 3 windows, preventing a noisy false positive rollback.

Review conversation (high level, single continuous narrative): Diego: "Nice approach; two asks: (1) add a small test for the cold-start of a new slice where sample count=0->n, and (2) open a follow-up to expose per-slice weights to the console for debugging." Asha: "Added cold-start unit test and an internal metrics hook; will follow up with a separate PR to expose weights in the public console (ENG-16003)." Mei: "Can we bound the smoothing alpha so we don't fully lock the detector during sustained traffic shift?" Asha: "Bounded to [0.1,0.8] and added tests for extremes." Samir: "CI flakes: the canary harness timed out on the second integration run." Asha: "Found flake in the synthetic driver; increased timeout and made scheduler idempotent; re-ran CI." After the rerun, Diego approved with "LGTM, non-blocking nit on doc wording," Mei approved, Samir approved.

CI: The PR adds a canary-suite job that runs a small set of end-to-end traces plus unit tests. First run had a transient harness timeout (integration job) which was fixed and the suite passed on re-run. CI checks: build/pass, unit-tests/pass, integration-canary-suite/pass, lint/pass, docs-check/pass.

Benchmarks: Local perf harness shows ensemble false positive rate reduced by ~45% on a simulated multi-cohort modal shift trace while detection latency for true regressions increased by ~1 window on average (configurable via smoothing alpha trade-off). Detailed numbers are in docs/perf/quantile_ensemble_bench.md.

Operational notes and runbook: The runbook outlines steps to inspect ensemble spread, how to force bypass the guard in emergency, and how to tune thresholds per-product. Default thresholds are conservative; ops can tune per-namespace.

Merge: squash and merge after approvals.
